rationale: Round 0 built and ran cleanly with no correctness or ICE issues, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up across the board. SUB is raised highest (0.9/0.85) because instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime and safe even in dense floating-point code like this flops-1 kernel, giving cheap security and diversity. SPLIT is boosted (0.8/0.75) since it is low-cost and enlarges the surface that BCF/FLA then obscure. BCF and FLA are increased to solidly attack control-flow recovery, but their RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights stay below ~0.4 because this is a tight numeric benchmark where per-iteration overhead dominates; FLA is kept slightly below BCF since flattening carries more loop-overhead risk in hot loops. IBR is raised moderately to break basic-block boundaries at acceptable cost. ICALL and IGV are raised the least and given the highest CorrectnessRisk weights (0.3/0.25): indirect calls and global-variable indirection interact most delicately with optimized floating-point code and a two-function binary (main/_start) where symbol indirection buys less diversity, so the selector applies them only where features strongly favor security. Overall the table trades a modest, controlled runtime/size budget for substantially stronger static reverse-engineering resistance, while keeping risk weights low enough to preserve the round-0 correctness result.
